description: Probe run (not a real attempt): random init, prints the task object's attributes to learn the prompt/answer format.
Probe run (not a real attempt): random init, prints sample task examples to learn padding and answer format.
1 block, no LN/pos: uniform attention counts ones, 10-ReLU MLP is a triangle wave of the count; 2 dims (count, odd).
1 block, d_model=1, no LN/pos: attention writes the count; residual slope +1 plus 9 ReLUs bends it into a +-1/2 zigzag.
d_model=1, d_ff=1, 4 blocks: attention writes the count, then 4 one-ReLU residual reflections at 5,3,2,1 fold [0,10] onto {0,1}, preserving parity.
No MLP/ReLU, 2 attention layers: first counts ones; second uses a quadratic bilinear score peaked at j=count to read a +-+- tape in position embeddings.
Pointer tape with one fewer dim: the read accumulates on the tape channel itself (2 even, 0 odd) and the head compares it to the constant channel.
10 blocks as a tiny CPU: block t points attention at position t, adds that bit to an accumulator, and one ReLU wraps it mod 2 (no counting step).
Attention only, 10 blocks: '=' carries a spin; block t compares bit t's key with its own so that it self-attends (and negates via W_v=-2) iff the bit is 1.
Log-depth XOR tree, 4 blocks: per-block pointer tables in position embeddings pair up cells, one ReLU per block does addition mod 2; no global count.
Unmodified 64d/4-head/3-block architecture with all LayerNorms: antisymmetric channels plus a constant reference make LN a known warp of the count; ReLU knots sit on the warped counts.
d_model=2 with LN as an exact comparator: count, then restoring subtraction of 8, 4, 2 (even, so parity survives) with 3 ReLU units; final LN compares against 0.5.
Same restoring subtraction of 8, 4, 2 in d_model=2, but the MLP is purely linear: LayerNorm is the only nonlinearity in the network.
One tied block applied 10 times like an RNN step: attention reads bit[PC] into ACC, one ReLU wraps ACC mod 2, and the MLP bias increments the program counter PC.
d_model=1: attention counts, then one tied 2-ReLU block runs 5 times as `while x >= 2: x -= 2`; +-1/2 are its fixed points.
d_model=1: attention writes count/16 - 1/2, then one tied 2-ReLU block iterates the tent map 4 times; T^4 is a triangle wave of period 2 in the count.
d_model=2, attention only, no LN or positions: softmax decides whether '=' attends to itself (x > k - 1/2), which subtracts k = 8, 4, 2 after counting.
d_model=2, attention only: after counting, one tied attention block runs 5 times as `while x > 3/2: x -= 2`, with '=' attending to itself as the test.
Deliberate negative control: attn_tied_sub2 with softmax sharpness BETA=3 instead of 30, to confirm the eval and exhaustive check can detect a broken comparator. Exhaustive check: 1034/2047.

One tied block run 15 times as the Rule 60 cellular automaton (every cell XORs its left neighbor); all C(15,d) are odd, so the '=' cell ends as the XOR of all bits. NOT actually perfect: 200-sample eval missed 3 errors, exhaustive check is 2044/2047; fixed in tied_rule60_beta60.
Rule 60 cellular automaton with a sharper pointer (BETA=60), testing whether the 3 exhaustive failures of tied_rule60_sierpinski came from attention leakage amplified over 15 steps.
d_model=2, one tied linear MLP block run 5 times with LayerNorm as the only nonlinearity: `while U > 3/2: U -= 2`, then the head compares U to a constant.
Accumulator scan with classic sinusoidal position embeddings: the pointer is a rotated query q.k = BETA cos(w(t-j)) instead of the quadratic score.
Accumulator scan with one-hot position keys and query e_t: W_q and W_k each have a single nonzero entry per block, the most literal form of 'block t reads position t'.
tied_tent_map with attention's four matrices removed: a fixed uniform causal average needs no parameters, so all remaining weights are embeddings, tent map or head.
Uniform attention then 3 blocks of 1, 1 and 2 ReLU units: folds at 5 and 3, then a 2-kink zigzag; (1+1)(1+1)(2+1)=12 pieces cover the 10 needed.
Two blocks of 3 and 2 ReLU units: a zigzag folds [0,10] onto [0,3], then a 2-kink zigzag finishes; (3+1)(2+1)=12 pieces, one more unit than the 3-layer version.

Predicted-to-fail test of the piece-count bound: two blocks of 2 and 2 ReLU units give (2+1)(2+1)=9 pieces, one short of 10; this construction should miss exactly count=4, i.e. 462 prompts. Exhaustive check: 1585/2047, as predicted.
Two ReLU units in total: uniform attention counts, one tied single-ReLU block applies x -> |x-2| five times, and one final ReLU applies |x-1| - 1/2 to separate evens from odds.

Predicted-partial-failure test: pointer_tape_d5 with BETA=1. A blurred +-+- read keeps its sign except where the tape is truncated, so counts 1 and 9 should fail: 66 prompts, 1981/2047. Exhaustive check: 1981/2047, as predicted; the 0.78 eval understates this.
pointer_tape_d5 with BETA=2, 10x softer: the same edge calculation predicts counts 1 and 9 now keep their sign, so a heavily blurred pointer should still be exact.
Real use of multi-head attention: each of 2 heads counts one 5-position window in parallel, MLPs reduce each to a parity, and a final block XORs them. Uses 10 ReLUs versus 4 for global folding.
